bib.title: Stochastic Linear Bandits with Finitely Many Arms (Chapter 22, Bandit Algorithms)
bib.venue: book chapter, Bandit Algorithms (Cambridge University Press)

question: With a fixed finite action set, can a phased-elimination policy built on a G-optimal design beat LinUCB's regret by a factor of sqrt(d)?
contributions: Algorithm 12 (phased elimination with G-optimal exploration) and Theorem 22.1 giving regret O(sqrt(dn log(nk))) for finite fixed action sets

results.claim: With a fixed finite action set of size k, Algorithm 12 has regret O(sqrt(dn log(nk))), improving LinUCB's O(d sqrt(n) log(n)) by a factor of d^(1/2) for moderate k.
results.setup: Stochastic linear bandit, |A|=k fixed over time, 1-subgaussian noise, gaps <= 1

results.claim: Each phase plays an optimal-design support of at most d(d+1)/2 arms, with arm a played T_l(a) = (2d pi_l(a)/eps_l^2) log(k l (l+1)/delta) times and eps_l = 2^-l.
Phase length is bounded by T_l <= (2d/eps_l^2) log(k l (l+1)/delta) + d(d+1)/2 (the additive term comes from rounding up the support).
results.note: Stated as an exercise to show, not proved in text

results.claim: With probability >= 1-delta the regret is <= C sqrt(n d log(k log(n)/delta)); with delta=O(1/n), E[Rn] <= C sqrt(nd log(kn)).
Changing action sets (|A_t|<=k) admit regret O(sqrt(nd log^3(nk))) via SupLinRel/SupLinUCB, but those algorithms are complicated and less practical than LinUCB or Thompson sampling.

limits: Requires a fixed (time-invariant) finite action set; the chapter says this assumption is crucial for Algorithm 12.
Proof of Theorem 22.1 is left to the reader (Exercise 22.1); no experiments, no figures, no worked numeric example.
Action choices in a phase depend only on earlier phases, so data within a phase is not used adaptively; this is the cost of the decoupling.
Requires solving a G-optimal design (max log det V) each phase; computation is not discussed.
practices: Use phase-based elimination: play arms by the G-optimal design for the surviving set, then eliminate arms whose estimated gap exceeds 2*eps_l (Algorithm 12, p.274).
Prefer LinUCB (Ch.19) or Thompson sampling (Ch.36) in practice when action sets change over time (p.275).
Choose delta=1/n to turn the high-probability bound into an expected-regret bound (p.274, Exercise 22.2).

terms.definition: A distribution pi in P(A_l) with support at most d(d+1)/2 maximising log det V(pi), used to choose exploration arms in each phase
At the end of a phase, arms likely to be suboptimal with a gap exceeding the current target are eliminated
